text: A restaurant booking is a promise that a seat will be ready for you. You pick a day, a time and how many people are coming, and the restaurant keeps a table free. Plans change, so people often ask to move the time, add a guest or cancel. They say things like 'make it eight instead of seven' or 'we are five now, not four'. Opening hours work in a similar way. If the road is busy or the weather is cool, many people check that the kitchen is still open before they leave. A menu lets you select a dish ahead of time, and you can ask for takeaway if you would rather eat at home.

name: voice_note_finder
does: Finds a spoken note you recorded earlier and plays it back so you can hear it again.
inputs: a few words about what the note was about, and roughly when you recorded it
people say:
- Play the note I made about the chair I want to buy
- Where is that large recording from last week
- I want to hear what I said about the garden
- Find my voice memo from Monday morning
- What did I record about the dentist

Marta the gardener came in from the peach trees with muddy boots. Earlier she had seen a strange car by the gate, and now she wanted the house kept safe while she worked outside, because later she planned to invite her sister for lunch. She stood in the hallway and said, 'Lock up.' The voice assistant understood she meant the doors. It locked the front and back doors, switched on the camera by the gate and told her both doors were secure. Marta nodded. 'Alarm too,' she added. The assistant set the alarm to stay mode, so the motion sensors in the yard would not ring while she moved around. She thanked it and went back to the garden.

Fuel is what keeps a car moving. The gauge on the dashboard shows how much is left, and the manual in the glove box tells you how big the tank is, often about fifty liters. People ask for small changes to what they do next: 'remind me to fill up when it is a quarter full' or 'find the nearest station'. Tyre pressure works in a similar way. If the warning light comes on, you check the pressure and add air. On a cold morning, many people ask the car to warm up for ten minutes before they leave, so they do not have to wipe the frost off the windows by hand.

Bread dough needs time to rise. Yeast makes small bubbles that puff the dough up, and a warm spot helps. A good baker will explain that the dough should double in size before it goes in the oven. People set timers for this and change them as they go: 'give it another ten minutes' or 'bake it five minutes less'. Oven heat matters too, and every recipe says how hot to make it. One baker who used to work at a hotel on the south coast always asked for a reminder to check the loaves halfway through. When the crust is golden and sounds hollow when you tap it, the bread is done.

A robot mower cuts the grass by itself. You choose the days and the hours it works, and when the battery runs low it drives back to its station. People change the plan often. They say 'skip the mowing tomorrow, the kids are playing' or 'cut the grass a bit shorter'. Sprinklers work in a similar way. A single timer decides when the water comes on, and you can ask it to stay off when rain is coming. On warm days the grass grows fast, and weeds climb along the edges. A neat edge makes the whole lawn look better. One neighbour says the mower beeps like a microwave when it finishes, which makes everyone laugh.

Time zones exist because the sun is not overhead everywhere at once. When it is bright noon in one city, it can be dark night in another. A phone shows the time where you are, and it can show other cities too. People add a place so they know when to call. Someone with a son studying far away might say 'what time is it in Tokyo' or 'is it too late to call him'. They also change the clock when summer time starts, saying 'move the clock forward one hour'. The phone usually does this by itself when you travel, so you rarely need to know how to set it by hand.

Person: Good morning. I would be very grateful if you could make me a packing list for the weekend, because last time I forgot my torch and had a miserable night.
Assistant: Happy to help. Which nights are you going, and will you sleep in a tent?
Person: Friday and Saturday, in a small tent. Some friends from the walking club will join me.
Assistant: Lovely. How cold will it get? I can check the hill weather if you tell me the place.
Person: Near the lake at Ridgeway. And please add something for my ears, the wind there makes them ache.
Assistant: I will add a warm hat and ear covers. The list so far: tent, sleeping bag, torch, spare batteries, stove, water and a daily snack bag. Shall I send it to your phone?
Person: Yes please, thank you.
Assistant: Done. The list is on your phone now.

Knitting is a slow hobby that fits into quiet evenings. You pick your wool, say blue for a scarf, and follow a pattern row by row. People count rows so they do not lose their place, and they ask to change the count: 'add one row' or 'go back two rows'. Many knitters start a big project in February, when the days are short, and hope to finish before spring. A timer can help you take a break, and you can ask it to remind you to put the work down and rest your hands. If you want to forward a pattern to a friend, you can send it as a message with a few kind words.

Sam woke up thirsty and stumbled into the kitchen with a bowl of lettuce for the rabbits. He could barely crack his eyes open, and then he remembered that the hot tub had gone cold overnight. 'Heat the tub to one hundred and two,' he mumbled to the speaker. The assistant understood that he meant degrees and that he wanted the hot tub, not the pool. It said it would start the heater now and that the water would be ready in about forty minutes. Sam thanked it, drank a big glass of water, fed the rabbits and went back to bed for a little while.

Someone wants to know how far they rode today.
How far did I go?
Distance, please
What's the total for my ride?
My legs are dead, so how many miles was that?
I'm hungry enough to empty a whole shelf of cakes, so did I earn it? Tell me how far I rode.
Tell me how many kilometres I covered this morning.
Did I go further than yesterday?
Could you please tell me the distance of the route I designed on Sunday?

A workout plan tells you which exercises to do, how many sets and how many reps. A set is a group of reps, like ten push-ups in a row, and between sets you rest. Rest days matter because muscles grow while they recover. People change the plan all the time: 'add one more set' or 'make today lighter'. Someone who has just left the hospital, or who is scared of getting hurt, might say 'go easy for a week'. An app can find a simpler routine and set a timer for each rest. A good plan is one you can follow every week, not one that wears you out.

Someone wants to know how many steps they have taken today.
Steps?
How many steps so far?
How far have I walked, and how many steps is that?
Give me my step count.
I want to know if I'm close to ten thousand.
I spend most of the day on my feet, so what's my total?
Counting my steps is the only task I have left today, can you do it?
My shoes feel loose, so tell me how much I've walked and how fast I went.
Could you tell me my steps and my pace for this morning?

Person: It's so quiet in here. I can never work this radio thing.
Assistant: I can turn the radio on for you. Which station would you like?
Person: I don't know the names. The one with the news in the morning.
Assistant: Do you mean the local news station or the national one?
Person: The local one. My neighbour says they earn prizes for their news.
Assistant: Good. I've tuned to Local News Radio and the news is playing.
Person: It sounds a bit raw and too loud. And there's a draft coming from the vent behind me. Can you shut it?
Assistant: I lowered the volume a little. I'm sorry, I can't control the vent. I can only play the radio and change the sound.

Priya got home after a twelve-hour night shift. The bedroom felt dry and stuffy, and her eyes hurt. She dropped her bag on the chair, caught sight of herself in the hall mirror and sighed. 'Turn the humidifier on high,' she said to the speaker. Then she changed her mind. 'No, wait, low. I want a soft hum so I can sleep.' The assistant understood the correction and set the humidifier in the bedroom to low. It also told her that the air purifier was already running quietly in the corner. Priya thanked it, closed the curtains and fell asleep within minutes.

Leo had moved to the city two days ago, and his phone was almost dead. He sat on the steps in the yard of his new building and said, 'My battery is dying, make it last.' The assistant turned on battery saver and lowered the screen brightness. Leo asked it to pair his earbuds, because he wanted to call his sister. The assistant found them nearby and connected them. It told him the battery was at nine percent and that a serious drain came from the map app, which it closed. When he got home, it said, he should charge the phone for twenty minutes. Leo smiled and made his call.

A pool pump moves the water through a filter so it stays clean. At home, most people run it on a timer, perhaps eight hours a day. When leaves make the water messy, they ask for the pump to run longer. If someone is swimming, they say 'pause the pump' and later 'resume the pump'. Water temperature works the same way. A hot tub is usually kept at around thirty-eight degrees, and people say 'make it a little warmer' or 'drop it by two degrees'. A cover keeps the heat in and the leaves out, so people also remind each other to put it back on.

Rest days are part of every good fitness plan. After hard workouts your body needs time to rebuild, so a plan often has a day with no exercise at all. People with busy weeks move these days around: 'make Wednesday my rest day' or 'skip tomorrow's workout'. A timer tells you when to stop a set, and a reminder can tell you when to start. Many people like to eat toast or fruit before a morning run for energy. If you feel tired, you can say 'make this week easier', and the plan can shorten the sessions or drop a set.

Someone wants to know the score of tonight's match.
Score?
Latest score
What's the score in the game?
Who's winning?
Is my team ahead right now?
Tell me how the match is going, I'm stuck at the sink doing dishes.
I had to borrow a small radio, so I can't see the screen. What's the score?
Could you please give me the score and tell me how much time is left?

Before a camping trip, people check the weather in the hills, because it can change quickly. A packing list helps you remember the tent, a stove to cook on, warm clothes and water. Many people keep the list on their phone and change it each time: 'add a rain jacket' or 'take off the second blanket'. Some go once a month and reuse the same list. A photo of the trail map saved on your phone works even without a signal. If the forecast says rain, people ask for a fresh forecast on the morning of the trip, saying 'will it rain on Saturday up there'.

Jay was sitting on the floor among half-filled boxes, texting his friend. His mom wanted the kitchen packed by dinner, but he would much rather swim at the pool. He had a bag of crispy chips in one hand and typed to the assistant with the other: 'ugh its been two hours and theres still no truck'. The assistant understood he wanted to know when the moving truck would arrive. It checked the movers' booking, told him the truck was due at four o'clock because the driver had been stuck in traffic, and sent him the driver's phone number. Jay sighed, put the chips down and went back to the boxes.

name: delay_alert
does: Watches a bus or train line and warns you when it is late or cancelled, so a stormy morning does not cost you an hour.
inputs: the line or route, and the time you plan to travel
people say:
- Is my train going to be late tonight
- Tell me if the seven fifteen bus gets held up
- Will the storm mess up my trip to work
- Warn me before I leave if the line is down
- I have no idea whether the trains are running

Dana was packing lunches and looking for a way to get the kids out of the house. 'What's on at the cinema tomorrow at four?' she asked her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted showtimes for a family film. It found a single cartoon at four called Moon Pirates and read out the times. Saving some money was on her mind, so she asked whether there was a cheaper ticket. The assistant said children's tickets were half price before five. Dana said she would need four tickets, two for the kids and two for the grown-ups. The assistant held four seats for tomorrow at four and sent the confirmation to her phone.

Omar woke up with a worry he could not name. Then he remembered: the electricity bill. He rubbed his eyes and said to his phone, 'Bills due?' The assistant understood he wanted to know what was coming up. It said the electricity bill of sixty dollars was due on Friday and the water bill was due next week. It also reminded him that his bank balance was low. Omar groaned, then smiled, remembering the story his dad always told about paying bills the day they arrive. He asked the assistant to remind him on Thursday morning, and it did. 'Thank you,' he said, and went to make coffee.

Ines ran a small fish shop and was waiting for a box of paper bags. Between customers she looked at her phone and said, 'Parcel status?' The assistant understood she wanted tracking for her latest order. It said the parcel was out for delivery and the driver would drop it off by noon. 'Sign for it?' she asked. The assistant explained that a signature was needed, so it would send her a message when the driver was at the door. 'Total items?' she asked next. The assistant said the box held three packs of bags, total weight four kilos. Ines thanked it and went back to wrapping a salmon.

Joining a work call is simple: you click a link, or you ask the assistant to open it at the right time. Inside the call, people adjust a few things, like the microphone, the camera and the volume. If someone sits far from the microphone, they say 'turn me up' or 'mute me for a minute'. Sharing a screen shows your slides to everyone, and you can say 'stop sharing' when you finish. An agenda lists the topics so the meeting stays short, and a good one gives each topic five minutes. A meeting that drags on can feel as heavy as a pound of bricks, so people say 'end the call at three'.

Person: Tide times?
Assistant: Sure. For which day?
Person: Tomorrow.
Assistant: High tide is at ten past nine in the morning and low tide is at three in the afternoon.
Person: Neat. I want to convert that into a sign for my shop window. Can you print it?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't print. I can send the times to your phone so you can copy them onto a sign.
Person: Yes, do that. And put the beach radio on in the shop.
Assistant: Done. The times are on your phone and the radio is playing.

Person: I posted a photo of my roses. I want more people to see it.
Assistant: Do you want me to share it again, or send it to your followers directly?
Person: Share it again. Double the reach if you can.
Assistant: I can share it again on your page, but I can't control how many people see it.
Person: That's fine. It's my dream garden, and the last post got only half the likes of the one before. I nearly cry when I think of the work. A tiny bit of attention would be nice.
Assistant: I'm sorry. I've shared it again. Would you like to add a few words?
Person: Yes: My dream garden in June.
Assistant: Added and posted.

A calendar keeps your plans in one place. A single event has a day, a start time and an end time, and many people add a place too. People move events often. They say 'push the meeting to Thursday' or 'make it an hour later'. Free time shows the gaps between events, and you can ask 'when am I free this week' to design a day around them. Some families still keep a paper calendar on the fridge, but a phone calendar can remind you before an event begins, say ten minutes ahead, so nothing is missed.

Person: Quick, I'm late. Set a nap alarm for the baby, but not the loud one.
Assistant: Of course. How many minutes should the nap be?
Person: Forty. And turn the monitor on.
Assistant: The alarm is set with a soft chime, and the monitor is on.
Person: Great. Now tell me what she should wear tonight, it's a total mystery to me.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't say what she should wear, but I can check tonight's temperature. It will be fourteen degrees.
Person: Then a thick sleepsuit. Not the one with the hamster on it, that's too thin.
Assistant: Good idea. I'll remind you at seven to lay out the thick one.

Someone wants to know what films are showing at the cinema.
What's on?
Anything good at the cinema?
Show me the movie times for tonight.
I'm bored and it's Thursday, so I wonder what's playing near me.
It's a sad grey evening and I'd love to get out of the house and see a film.
Is there a cinema where I can park easily and see something tonight?
Could you please tell me what's on at the cinema this weekend?
Any new releases?

When you order something online, the shop packs it and a driver brings it to your door. You choose a size and a delivery day, and you can change them before it ships. People ask 'make it a medium' or 'send it to my work address instead'. If an item does not fit, returning it is simple: you show a code and drop the parcel at a shop. Some drivers leave parcels by the gate if no one is home, so people say 'leave it with the neighbour'. If you are sorry you bought something, you can ask for your money back within a few weeks.

name: address_change_helper
does: Tells the right places about your new address, like the bank, the post office and the electric company, so nothing gets lost.
inputs: the new address, the date you move, and which places should be told
people say:
- I'm moving next month, tell everyone my new address
- Change my mail to the new house
- Make sure the electric company knows I'm leaving on the first
- Mom needs my new address for her cards, can you send it
- Tell the pet shop where to send the cat feed
- I got the cool new flat on Oak Street, so change my address everywhere

Hana ran a flower shop and drove a small van. One morning the van pulled to the left and she felt uneasy. 'Check my tyre pressure,' she said to the car. The assistant answered that the front right tyre was low, at twenty-six when it should be thirty-two. Her mouth fell open. 'Make sure I get a reminder, I prefer to keep them a little higher in winter, because I carry heavy buckets,' she said. The assistant set a reminder to check all four tyres in a week and showed the nearest air pump, two minutes away. Hana added half a bar of air and drove off to deliver the roses.

Someone wants to know when their homework is due.
When's it due?
What homework do I have?
Tell me my assignments for this week.
Remind me about the essay.
I'm in a stormy mood about school, so just tell me what is due first.
Has my teacher set anything new?
Could you ask the speaker on my desk to read out my homework list, the one with the twenty-five questions?
Please tell me which assignment has the closest due date, because I want to start with that one.

Tom the gardener came in with muddy boots, and a rainy week had tracked dirt across the whole hall. He pulled off his boots and said to the speaker, 'Run the vacuum tomorrow at seven.' The assistant understood that he meant the robot vacuum and set it for seven in the morning. It added the job to the cleaning schedule and said the robot would do the hall first. 'Skip the bedroom,' Tom added. 'My wife sleeps late on Saturdays.' The assistant removed the bedroom from the job, and told him the robot would be finished by half past eight. Tom nodded and went to wash his hands.

Rosa ran a gift shop and had a video call with her supplier in ten minutes. She was stacking boxes when she typed to her phone: 'join the meeitng at 3'. The assistant understood what she meant in spite of the typo. It opened the link from her calendar for the supplier meeting at three and turned the microphone on. The call was about an event for new candles, and she wanted to hear the first voice message from the supplier before it started, so she asked it to play that message. She also asked it to turn the volume down a little, because less noise helps in a busy shop. The assistant did both, and Rosa joined the call on time.

Mr. Wells wanted a hotel room in a village by the sea. He held his phone a little away from his face and said, 'Book a room for two nights.' Then he frowned. 'No, three nights. My wife says three.' The assistant understood the correction. It found a small hotel in the village with a free breakfast and asked how many guests there would be. 'Two,' he said. Then he asked whether the room had a kettle, because he liked to boil his own water for tea. The assistant said yes. It booked three nights for two guests and read the check-in time out loud, which was after two in the afternoon.

In a board game, a score is a number that tells you who is winning. Players write it on paper or ask a phone to keep it. Scores change fast, so people say 'add three points for Mia' or 'take one away'. A timer is useful for word games: you set it for a minute and shout when the sand runs out. Rules can be confusing, and people ask 'how many cards do I draw'. In the middle of a game, someone might need a break, so the timer is paused. One family keeps score on the back of a shop receipt, which works well until somebody spills the juice.

Eli was eight and hungry. His mom had left dough in a tray, and he stood on a stool by the oven and said, 'How long do I bake the bread? Don't rush me, and I don't want it burnt.' The assistant understood that he wanted the baking time, and it did not rush him. It told him to bake the bread for twenty minutes at two hundred degrees and asked him to wait until the oven beeped. Then it set a timer. When it rang, the bread was warm and golden, and Eli's mom helped him take it out. 'I did it,' he said. The assistant said it smelled wonderful.

Grace finished her night shift at seven and wanted a short walk before going to sleep. The morning was chilly, and she pulled her scarf tight. 'Track a walk, about three miles,' she told her watch. Then she shook her head. 'Sorry, two miles. I'm too tired.' The assistant changed the goal to two miles and started tracking. It said it would notify her when she reached the halfway mark. On the way she passed her bank, where she had planned to ask about a loan, so she asked the assistant to remind her to call them in the afternoon. It set the reminder for two o'clock.

Someone wants to know how many words their essay has.
Word count?
How long is my essay?
How many words are in this, and how many pages?
Count the words for me.
I need to increase the length, so how many words do I have now?
A bulb went on in my head about the ending, but first tell me how many words I have so far.
My teacher is bitter about short essays, so please check my length and my spelling.
Could you please count the words in my draft so I know whether I have reached the limit?

Mr. Alvarez, a retired teacher, stood at the sink washing his hands with soap and thinking about dinner. He said to the speaker, 'Find a table for two at an Italian place tonight. I don't want anywhere noisy, and not too far.' The assistant found a quiet Italian restaurant ten minutes away and asked for a time. 'Seven is fine,' he said. The assistant booked a table for two at seven and told him there would be no wait if he arrived on time. It also showed him the menu on his phone. Mr. Alvarez dried his hands and went to find his coat.

Nina was a student with a desk covered in glue sticks and paper for a school project. Her hands were sticky, so she said, 'Text Amir that I'll be there tomorrow at seven.' The assistant understood she meant Amir from her group chat and wrote the message for her. She added, 'Tell him I'll bring the posters. His dad said he will fry rice for everyone.' The assistant added that line and read the whole message back to her. She said it was fine. It sent the text inside the group chat so everyone could see it, and Nina went back to her glue.

Someone wants to find a note they wrote last week.
Find my note from last week
Where did I put that note about the plumber?
Show notes from Tuesday
Not the shopping list, the other one about the trip.
That heavy note about the budget, can you open it?
My guests arrive soon and I need the note with the recipe link.
Could you please look through my notes for the one with the word garage in it?

Kai was nine years old, and in March his class would go on a long hike. He wanted new boots, so he asked the tablet, 'Can I get these boots in a bigger size?' The assistant understood that he meant the boots on the shopping page. At the bottom of the page it showed size three, and Kai asked for one size bigger. The assistant changed it to size four. It said the boots were half price today and that delivery would take two days. Just then his phone buzzed with a message from his mom, who said yes. The assistant placed the order.

name: burn_care_steps
does: Gives short steps for treating a small burn at home and says when to call for help, so you can avoid a pricey trip to the clinic when you do not need one.
inputs: where the burn is, how big it is, and what caused it
people say:
- I touched the hot pan, what do I do
- My hand is red and stings from the kettle
- How long should I run cold water on this
- Should I lift the cloth off the burn
- The driver of our van burned his arm on the engine, help

Mia was texting from the couch while the television murmured in the background. She was supposed to meet friends at nine, and her legs still ached from a morning jog. She typed: 'my feet are killing me and its too far to walk'. The assistant understood that she wanted a ride. It asked for the pickup point, and she wrote 'the front door'. It booked a car that would arrive in eight minutes and showed her the driver's name. She added, 'tell him not to call, im in a quiet house'. The assistant passed the note to the driver, and Mia put on her shoes.

Carla was a busy parent packing for a trip with her son. 'Book a hotel room in Lisbon for three nights,' she said while folding shirts. The assistant asked how many guests there would be. 'Three. Me, my son and my mother,' she said. It found a room with an extra bed and placed a temporary hold on it. The hold would last fifteen minutes, so she had time to check her husband's dates. A few minutes later he sent a message saying the dates were fine. Carla told the assistant to confirm, and it booked the room and sent her the details.

Someone wants the phone to read a message out loud.
Read it out
Read my messages to me
Can you say that text out loud?
I can't see the screen well, so read it.
What does the monthly bill email say?
Both my hands are covered in vinegar from cleaning, so please read the new message aloud.
Could you read me the screen? I tend to hide my glasses and can never find them.
Excuse me, I would be very thankful if you could read my new messages out loud, because my eyes are tired after a long day and the small writing gives me a headache.
